LESSON: THE PERIODIC TABLE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Matter and Chemical Reactions
Topic 2.1: The Periodic Table
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Periodic Table, part of Matter and Chemical Reactions in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why is electron arrangement significant? 2. How are elements arranged in the periodic table?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. carry out activities to review the concepts of the structure of an atom, atomic number, mass number and the electron arrangement of atoms of selected elements and share with peers. Learners with manipulation difficulties could be supported by peers, learner support assistants or teachers to carry out experiments,

2. arrange the first 20 elements using similarities in their electron arrangements. Learners with short stature, on wheelchairs and those using adapted seats, tables or positioning devices could be appropriately positioned or be provided with height-adjustable surfaces to carry out the activity of arrangement. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. carry out activities to review the concepts of the structure of an atom, atomic number, mass number and the electron arrangement of atoms of selected elements and share with peers. Learners with manipulation difficulties could be supported by peers, learner support assistants or teachers to carry out experiments,
2. arrange the first 20 elements using similarities in their electron arrangements. Learners with short stature, on wheelchairs and those using adapted seats, tables or positioning devices could be appropriately positioned or be provided with height-adjustable surfaces to carry out the activity of arrangement. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Periodic Table together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: as the learner sorts and arranges the first twenty elements of the periodic table

according to their similarities.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner models the electron configuration of any five elements of the periodic table

using locally available materials.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner recognises and respects the input of every group member as they discuss how to determine the

valence and oxidation numbers of elements and radicals.

● Unity: as the learner takes turns in playing roles when drawing dot (.) and cross (x) diagrams to illustrate ion formation

for atoms of elements of the periodic table.

● Responsibility: as the learner uses digital devices appropriately to watch simulations and animations on ion formation.

34

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Life skills – Problem solving skills: as the learner arranges the first twenty elements of the periodic table into groups

and periods.

● Financial literacy: as the learner uses locally available materials as a way of minimising the expenses when modelling

the electron configuration of any five elements of the periodic table.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Textbook, Periodic table chart, locally available materials (such as Cardboard or manilla paper, wires or strings, plasticine,

beads or bottle tops), Online resources, educational videos, interactive simulations, adapted digital devices, Adapted

writing resources,
